<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.11</span> Flat Torsion-Free Connections (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/torsion-curvature.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Torsion_Curvature">6.4</a>)</h1></header>
<p><strong>Proposition.</strong> A torsion-free connection satisfies <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem} = 0\)</span> on an open set <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{W}\)</span> if and only if around every <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{W}\)</span> there is a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\)</span>.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p><strong>(<span class="math inline">\(\Leftarrow\)</span>)</strong> If <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\)</span>, the component functions of <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}\)</span> vanish in <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span> (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a>), so the tensor field <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}\)</span> vanishes on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{V}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>(<span class="math inline">\(\Rightarrow\)</span>) Parallel covector fields.</strong> Take a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\)</span> with <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}(p) = 0\)</span>, a cube <span class="math inline">\(C = (-r, r)^d \subseteq \mathscr{X}(\mathcal{U} \cap \mathcal{W})\)</span>, and write component functions as functions of the coordinates <span class="math inline">\(\alpha \in C\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k \coloneqq \partial / \partial \alpha^k\)</span>. A covector field <span class="math inline">\(\mathsf{X} = \mathtt{x}_i \, dx^i\)</span> is parallel, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla \mathsf{X} = 0\)</span>, if  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i = \Gamma^j_{ik} \, \mathtt{x}_j, \qquad \forall \, i, k. \tag{P}
        \end{align*}</span>  Differentiating (P) and using it again, <span class="math inline">\(0 = \partial_m \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i - \partial_k \partial_m \mathtt{x}_i = \mathrm{Riem}^j_{imk} \, \mathtt{x}_j\)</span>, so flatness is exactly the condition for (P) to be solvable with arbitrary values at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. Explicitly, solve the <span class="math inline">\(k = 1\)</span> equation along the <span class="math inline">\(\alpha^1\)</span>-axis, then the <span class="math inline">\(k = 2\)</span> equation along <span class="math inline">\(\alpha^2\)</span> from every point reached, and so on up to <span class="math inline">\(k = d\)</span>, each step being a linear system of ordinary differential equations with a unique smooth solution on <span class="math inline">\((-r, r)\)</span>. After step <span class="math inline">\(s\)</span>, the defect <span class="math inline">\(w_i \coloneqq \partial_k \mathtt{x}_i - \Gamma^j_{ik} \mathtt{x}_j\)</span> of any earlier equation, <span class="math inline">\(k &lt; s\)</span>, satisfies  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            \partial_s w_i = \Gamma^j_{is} \, w_j - \mathrm{Riem}^j_{isk} \, \mathtt{x}_j = \Gamma^j_{is} \, w_j,
        \end{align*}</span>  with <span class="math inline">\(w_i = 0\)</span> at <span class="math inline">\(\alpha^s = 0\)</span>, hence <span class="math inline">\(w_i = 0\)</span>: all equations of (P) hold on <span class="math inline">\(C\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Parallel coframe.</strong> Starting from <span class="math inline">\((d\mathscr{X}^a)_p\)</span>, this yields parallel covector fields <span class="math inline">\(\mathsf{X}^a = \mathtt{x}^a_{i} \, dx^i\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(a = 1, \dots, d\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\det(\mathtt{x}^a_{i}) = 1\)</span> at <span class="math inline">\(\alpha = 0\)</span>, hence non-zero on <span class="math inline">\(C\)</span> after shrinking <span class="math inline">\(r\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Coordinates.</strong> Since <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> is torsion-free, <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma^j_{ik} = \Gamma^j_{ki}\)</span>, so (P) gives <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k \mathtt{x}^a_{i} = \partial_i \mathtt{x}^a_{k}\)</span>. On <span class="math inline">\(C\)</span>, the functions  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            F^a(\alpha) \coloneqq \int_0^1 \mathtt{x}^a_{i}(\lambda \alpha) \, \alpha^i \, d\lambda
            \qquad \text{satisfy} \qquad
            \partial_k F^a(\alpha) = \int_0^1 \frac{d}{d\lambda} \Big[ \lambda \, \mathtt{x}^a_{k}(\lambda \alpha) \Big] d\lambda = \mathtt{x}^a_{k}(\alpha),
        \end{align*}</span>  where the symmetry was used to recognize the total derivative. The Jacobian of <span class="math inline">\(F\)</span> is <span class="math inline">\((\mathtt{x}^a_{k})\)</span>, invertible, so by the inverse function theorem <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{Y}^a \coloneqq F^a \circ \mathscr{X}\)</span> defines a chart <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span> around <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> in the maximal atlas, with <span class="math inline">\(d\mathscr{Y}^a = \mathtt{x}^a_{k} \, dx^k = \mathsf{X}^a\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Vanishing coefficients.</strong> In <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\)</span>, the parallel covector fields <span class="math inline">\(dy^a\)</span> have constant component functions <span class="math inline">\(\delta^a_i\)</span>, so <span class="math inline">\(0 = \big( \nabla_{\partial y_k} dy^a \big)_i = - \left( \Gamma_\mathscr{Y} \right)^a_{ik}\)</span> for all <span class="math inline">\(a, i, k\)</span>. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p></li>
<li><p><strong>Remarks.</strong> Torsion-freeness is necessary: <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma_\mathscr{Y} = 0\)</span> implies <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{T} = 0\)</span>, so charts with <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma = 0\)</span> exist if and only if <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem} = 0\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathtt{T} = 0\)</span>. The result is local: a flat torus, for instance, admits such charts around every point but no global one. Two such charts differ by an affine change of coordinates, since their transition map has vanishing second derivatives by the transformation law.</p></li>
</ul>
